It's a sliding-window rate limiter keyed by string, such as a user ID or IP address. `tryAcquire(key)` allows at most `limit` calls per key in any rolling `windowMilliseconds` period.

Each call drops the key's timestamps that are older than the window. If `limit` or more remain, it returns `false`. Otherwise it records the current time and returns `true`. You can pass `now` to make it easy to test.

A key's timestamps are only cleaned up when that key is used again, and keys are never removed from the map. So if you have many one-off keys, such as IP addresses, memory will keep growing.
